The dataset was generated by the generator in our internal benchmark project on Spark. Hope it will be open sourced later.

在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8下午1时39分05秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：

> On Wed, Oct 29, 2014 at 7:23 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > reduceByKey () currently supports setting of the number of partitions. I have changed the number of partitions when I was running the wordcount example.
> >
> > comparison with pySpark: on the same dataset, it takes pySpark ~35 seconds to complete. 2x slower than the native scala version. not so bad:)
> >
> Is this dataset available somewhere or is there a particular process to generate it ? It would be interesting to profile how much time is spent in different parts of SparkR to figure out where we can make improvements.
>
> Thanks
> Shivaram
> > 在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8上午1时52分30秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > Thanks for benchmarking -- I think there are a couple of things here that affect performance, and can be improved.
> > >
> > > - Number of reducers: The default value gives bad performance and we should set the default number based on number of partitions in the previous RDD. Hao Lin actually did this for `distinct`, but we need to do it for reduceByKey as well.
> > >
> > > - Benchmark programs: One of the big bottlenecks in the word count example is that the performance of computing hashCode on strings is very slow. It would be great to also run Logistic Regression to get another data point which doesn't use string-keys for shuffle. (FYI The hashCode performance improvement is being tracked in https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-87)
> > >
> > > - Comparison with Spark: While its useful to compare against Scala version of Spark, I think we should also compare with PySpark which has a similar architecture. That would help us figure out where our overheads are in SparkR code vs. the architecture decisions
> > >
> > > Thanks
> > > Shivaram
> > >
> > > On Tue, Oct 28, 2014 at 6:58 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > It makes no sense to spark.driver.memory here. Use SPARK_MEM. In sparkR.R, you can see code:
> > > >   sparkMem <- Sys.getenv("SPARK_MEM", "512m")
> > > >   .sparkREnv$libname <- libname
> > > >   .sparkREnv$assemblyJarPath <- assemblyJarPath
> > > >   .jinit(classpath=assemblyJarPath, parameters=paste("-Xmx", sparkMem, sep=""))
> > > >
> > > > which picks SPARK_MEM to initialize the JVM max heap size when .jinit is called to launch a JVM.
> > > >
> > > > 在 2014年10月29日星期三UTC+8上午7时14分14秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > I changed reduceByKey to take 10L and it now reduce time to half. Thank you very much for your help.
> > > > > I also tried to set driver memory using SPARK_MEM from command line but it not picking up that memory :
> > > > > SPARK_HOME=/usr/lib/spark SPARK_MEM=5g /home/user/SparkR-pkg-master/sparkR /home/userSparkR-pkg-master/examples/wordcount.R then I made changes in inti()
> > > > > inside code : sc <- sparkR.init(master="spark://master:7077", "SparkRWordCount100000kb", ,sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g")) this able to pick driver memory as spark env variables on each executor.
> > > > >
> > > > > also added cache(lines) to load data in memory
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On 28 October 2014 14:24, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Hi, Nahak,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > currently SparkR is really slow. I ran the wordcount example with 3.2G data on a 3-slave spark cluster (16 logical CPUs and 48G memory per node) and it took 3.8 hours to complete. After I enabled map-side reduction, the time was shortened to 1.6 hours. While a scala version of wordcount only takes 17 seconds on the same dataset. You can try the following steps to see if the performance can be improved:
> > > > > > 1. Pull the latest code in which map-side reduction in reduceByKey() has been enabled;
> > > > > > 2. set driver memory using SPARK_MEM variable;
> > > > > > 3. Modify the wordcount source code:
> > > > > >   sc <- sparkR.init(args[[1]], "RwordCount", , sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g"))
> > > > > > 4. Modify the wordcount source code to increase the reducer number for reduceByKey():
> > > > > >   counts <- reduceByKey(wordCount, "+", 10L)
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 在 2014年10月28日星期二UTC+8上午8时44分36秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > > > I was running a 100 MB file for wordcount given in sparkR examples and it took 1 hr 40 mins to complete. In same cluster when we compute MLllib SVD computation on 20 GB it completes on an hour. i.e.. spark clusters works as expected but same not with SparkR . Here is my cluster and app details , this might be a case :
> > > > > > >   >  1 master node of 16 GB memory with 4 cores {excluded from workers list}
> > > > > > >   >  3 workers,  Worker 1 has 4 cores/16g memory and Worker 2&3 have 2 cores/8g memory.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Environment settings: spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g" and reading input file from hdfs with 128 MB block size.
> > > > > > > screenshot of Worker 1 when application is running :
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > ​
> > > > > > > Any clue, is this the cluster issue or need to do something from R side?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On 25 October 2014 01:52, hao lin <hlin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > I guess we could batch the R list partitions into smaller blocks, if necessary.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Thursday, October 23, 2014 10:44:20 PM UTC-4, hipho...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > > It's OK to add persist(storageLevel) API to the RDD class. What I am concerned is that for large data sets, R worker may be a bottleneck because it loads the partition data entirely into memory as a list for processing. So if the partition data can't fit in memory in R worker, I am not sure about the behavior of R.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > 在 2014年10月23日星期四UTC+8下午10时48分09秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：

> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > Shivaram
> > > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > > > > Just figure out , using cache() we can do this, but by default its store in MEMORY, how we can make it to MEMORY_AND_DISK? because I've more than 10 GB of file for processing.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, 23 October 2014 16:20:16 UTC+13, hna...@wynyardgroup.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > > > > > > > > I'm running SparkR on Apche Spark 1.1.0. while running workcount.R for 1 Gb input file, what I observed is it never store RDD in memory or disk. I checked in Executor tab which shows memory and disk used in each Executor, it always shows 0.0 B used.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > In scala I can used rows.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)   , can we do the same thing in R as well ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > --Harihar

You are right. When I run my job through command prompt using MASTER URL it executes on cluster in parallel mode.

But when tried it through SparkR shell by setting explicitly spark context to MASTER URL, it is not executing in parallel.

I observed, if I print sc there is no change before and after setting spark context to MASTER.

Best,
Nilesh Patil

messages.body_plain:
Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui> commented on  SPARKR-133 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-133>

Re: Unable to run parallel jobs when submitted through SparkR shell <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-133>

I realized that sparkR.init() will cache its created SparkContext , and subsequent calls to sparkR.init() won't return new SparkContexts but the cached one. So you can either:

MASTER=<spark master URL> ./sparkR

or modifiy the source code to remove the logic to cache the created SparkContext, and then call sparkR.init() to create a new SparkContext.

messages.body_plain:
By default the example assumes there are 10 dimensions in the data set [1]. You'll need to update this to 4 for this dataset. (We should probably make this a command line argument. Feel free to send a PR if you make that change).

Thanks
Shivaram

[1] https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/blob/master/examples/logistic_regression.R#L13

On Sun Nov 02 2014 at 7:36:11 PM Harihar Nahak <hna...@wynyardgroup.com> wrote:

> Thanks. I'll wait for that. This weekend I tried running logistics_regrassion.R , to verify the performance when we compute or process integer/long values. It was failing for couple of matrix I've given on Matrix manipulation.
>
> so I've change data set to https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/00267/data_banknote_authentication.txt it looks more authentic but still it fall in with same exception :
> in R worker logs  :
> 14/11/03 16:18:12 WARN NativeCodeLoader: Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable
> Error in X %*% w : non-conformable arguments
> Calls: do.call ... func -> FUN -> FUN -> Reduce -> <Anonymous> -> FUN -> FUN
> Execution halted
> Error in X %*% w : non-conformable arguments
> Calls: do.call ... func -> FUN -> FUN -> Reduce -> <Anonymous> -> FUN -> FUN
> Execution halted
> 14/11/03 16:18:18 ERROR Executor: Exception in task 0.0 in stage 0.0 (TID 0)
> java.lang.NullPointerException
>
> I think it is something related to input matrix which I'm giving. Do you guys have any input data set to run with ?
>
>
>
> On 1 November 2014 20:57, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > The dataset was generated by the generator in our internal benchmark project on Spark. Hope it will be open sourced later.
> >
> > 在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8下午1时39分05秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > On Wed, Oct 29, 2014 at 7:23 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > reduceByKey () currently supports setting of the number of partitions. I have changed the number of partitions when I was running the wordcount example.
> > > >
> > > > comparison with pySpark: on the same dataset, it takes pySpark ~35 seconds to complete. 2x slower than the native scala version. not so bad:)
> > > >
> > > Is this dataset available somewhere or is there a particular process to generate it ? It would be interesting to profile how much time is spent in different parts of SparkR to figure out where we can make improvements.
> > >
> > > Thanks
> > > Shivaram
> > > > 在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8上午1时52分30秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > > > Thanks for benchmarking -- I think there are a couple of things here that affect performance, and can be improved.
> > > > >
> > > > > - Number of reducers: The default value gives bad performance and we should set the default number based on number of partitions in the previous RDD. Hao Lin actually did this for `distinct`, but we need to do it for reduceByKey as well.
> > > > >
> > > > > - Benchmark programs: One of the big bottlenecks in the word count example is that the performance of computing hashCode on strings is very slow. It would be great to also run Logistic Regression to get another data point which doesn't use string-keys for shuffle. (FYI The hashCode performance improvement is being tracked in https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-87)
> > > > >
> > > > > - Comparison with Spark: While its useful to compare against Scala version of Spark, I think we should also compare with PySpark which has a similar architecture. That would help us figure out where our overheads are in SparkR code vs. the architecture decisions
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks
> > > > > Shivaram
> > > > >
> > > > > On Tue, Oct 28, 2014 at 6:58 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > It makes no sense to spark.driver.memory here. Use SPARK_MEM. In sparkR.R, you can see code:
> > > > > >   sparkMem <- Sys.getenv("SPARK_MEM", "512m")
> > > > > >   .sparkREnv$libname <- libname
> > > > > >   .sparkREnv$assemblyJarPath <- assemblyJarPath
> > > > > >   .jinit(classpath=assemblyJarPath, parameters=paste("-Xmx", sparkMem, sep=""))
> > > > > >
> > > > > > which picks SPARK_MEM to initialize the JVM max heap size when .jinit is called to launch a JVM.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 在 2014年10月29日星期三UTC+8上午7时14分14秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > > > I changed reduceByKey to take 10L and it now reduce time to half. Thank you very much for your help.
> > > > > > > I also tried to set driver memory using SPARK_MEM from command line but it not picking up that memory :
> > > > > > > SPARK_HOME=/usr/lib/spark SPARK_MEM=5g /home/user/SparkR-pkg-master/sparkR /home/userSparkR-pkg-master/examples/wordcount.R then I made changes in inti()
> > > > > > > inside code : sc <- sparkR.init(master="spark://master:7077", "SparkRWordCount100000kb", ,sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g")) this able to pick driver memory as spark env variables on each executor.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > also added cache(lines) to load data in memory
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On 28 October 2014 14:24, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > Hi, Nahak,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > currently SparkR is really slow. I ran the wordcount example with 3.2G data on a 3-slave spark cluster (16 logical CPUs and 48G memory per node) and it took 3.8 hours to complete. After I enabled map-side reduction, the time was shortened to 1.6 hours. While a scala version of wordcount only takes 17 seconds on the same dataset. You can try the following steps to see if the performance can be improved:
> > > > > > > > 1. Pull the latest code in which map-side reduction in reduceByKey() has been enabled;
> > > > > > > > 2. set driver memory using SPARK_MEM variable;
> > > > > > > > 3. Modify the wordcount source code:
> > > > > > > >   sc <- sparkR.init(args[[1]], "RwordCount", , sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g"))
> > > > > > > > 4. Modify the wordcount source code to increase the reducer number for reduceByKey():
> > > > > > > >   counts <- reduceByKey(wordCount, "+", 10L)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 在 2014年10月28日星期二UTC+8上午8时44分36秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > > > > > I was running a 100 MB file for wordcount given in sparkR examples and it took 1 hr 40 mins to complete. In same cluster when we compute MLllib SVD computation on 20 GB it completes on an hour. i.e.. spark clusters works as expected but same not with SparkR . Here is my cluster and app details , this might be a case :
> > > > > > > > >   >  1 master node of 16 GB memory with 4 cores {excluded from workers list}
> > > > > > > > >   >  3 workers,  Worker 1 has 4 cores/16g memory and Worker 2&3 have 2 cores/8g memory.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Environment settings: spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g" and reading input file from hdfs with 128 MB block size.
> > > > > > > > > screenshot of Worker 1 when application is running :
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > ​
> > > > > > > > > Any clue, is this the cluster issue or need to do something from R side?

> > > > > > > > > On 25 October 2014 01:52, hao lin <hlin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > I guess we could batch the R list partitions into smaller blocks, if necessary.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, October 23, 2014 10:44:20 PM UTC-4, hipho...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > It's OK to add persist(storageLevel) API to the RDD class. What I am concerned is that for large data sets, R worker may be a bottleneck because it loads the partition data entirely into memory as a list for processing. So if the partition data can't fit in memory in R worker, I am not sure about the behavior of R.
> > > > > > > > > > >

Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> commented on  SPARKR-133 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-133>

Re: Unable to run parallel jobs when submitted through SparkR shell <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-133>

Yeah, sparkR.init caches the spark context created as its usually not a good idea to have multiple SparkContexts from the same process. This is mainly because things like cached RDDs, web UI ports etc. are all SparkContext specific, so it could be confusing if we create an RDD and then reinitialize the SparkContext etc.

We could print a warning / info message saying "Re-using existing SparkContext" if that would be helpful.

Also there is a another way Nilesh Patil <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=NSP> you could use that might be useful to document. You can just launch R and then run something like

   library(SparkR, lib.loc="<path to where SparkR was installed">)
   sc <- sparkR.init(master="<spark master URL>", ...)

>From the error message it looks like the Spark client was not able to connect to the Spark cluster. This could happen due to a few reasons

1. The Spark versions running on the SparkR driver and cluster are different. You can check this by verifying the Spark version being included in the maven build.

I think there are configuration options that allow one to control what the driver hostname and ports to use should be (See the networking section in http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html) but I haven't tried it out before.

Nilesh Patil <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=nsp> Thanks a lot for sending the stack trace. There is an assumption in SparkR that the library is installed in the same location in the driver and in the cluster. Obviously this will not be true for driver program on windows connecting to a Linux cluster.

I've created a PR (https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/103) that will allow you to pass in sparkRLibDir while calling sparkR.init. You can pass the directory SparkR is installed in the cluster using this. For example on my Macbook, SparkR is installed at /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library/SparkR. So I'll need to pass /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library as sparkRLibDir.

Let me know if this helps.

Hi Guys,

 Here are some interesting statistics i got from logistics_regression.R, I hope this will help to understand that there is something specific need to fix for String operations.

In word count example my setup took:

100 MB  took 1.20 hours
1 GB was failed

in logistic_regression example:

Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> created an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-135> SPARKR-135 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-135>
Improve word count performance <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-135>
Issue Type:    Improvement
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   Internals
Created:   10/Nov/14 10:40 PM
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram>

The word count example in SparkR is very slow for small inputs and fails for larger inputs as described in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/sparkr-dev/R5mcbMnw9MY/discussion

We should profile and improve the performance of hashing and shuffling strings

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

sample data set available in this link https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/00267/data_banknote_authentication.txt
However it is just few MB in size and 4 columns + 1 category column, similarly I create bigger size using excel randombetween(-10,10) * rand() and generate different size of data sets.

If anyways I can upload this data set, just let me know I'll happy to share.

--Harihar

On 12 November 2014 14:38, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Harihar, could you tell me where you got the data sets for the logitstic_regression example? I'd like to have a try.
>
> 在 2014年11月11日星期二UTC+8下午12时49分24秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > Hi Guys,
> >
> >  Here are some interesting statistics i got from logistics_regression.R, I hope this will help to understand that there is something specific need to fix for String operations.
> >
> > In word count example my setup took:
> >
> > 100 MB  took 1.20 hours
> > 1 GB was failed
> >
> > in logistic_regression example:
> > File Size       - No. of rows in file             - No. of dimension/columns => time taken
> > 70 MB file     - 500 thousands  rows    - 12 dimensions   => 17 seconds
> > 547 MB file   - 1 million rows                - 12 dimensions  =>  27 seconds
> > 1.4GB file     - 10 million rows              - 12 dimensions  => 1.6 mins
> > 14 GB file     - 100 million rows            - 12 dimensions  => 14 mins
> >
> >  Thanks,
> > Harihar
> >
> > On 3 November 2014 16:35, Harihar Nahak <hna...@wynyardgroup.com> wrote:
> > > Thanks. I'll wait for that. This weekend I tried running logistics_regrassion.R , to verify the performance when we compute or process integer/long values. It was failing for couple of matrix I've given on Matrix manipulation.
> > >
> > > so I've change data set to https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/00267/data_banknote_authentication.txt it looks more authentic but still it fall in with same exception :
> > > in R worker logs  :
> > > 14/11/03 16:18:12 WARN NativeCodeLoader: Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable
> > > Error in X %*% w : non-conformable arguments
> > > Calls: do.call ... func -> FUN -> FUN -> Reduce -> <Anonymous> -> FUN -> FUN
> > > Execution halted
> > > Error in X %*% w : non-conformable arguments
> > > Calls: do.call ... func -> FUN -> FUN -> Reduce -> <Anonymous> -> FUN -> FUN
> > > Execution halted
> > > 14/11/03 16:18:18 ERROR Executor: Exception in task 0.0 in stage 0.0 (TID 0)
> > > java.lang.NullPointerException
> > >
> > > I think it is something related to input matrix which I'm giving. Do you guys have any input data set to run with ?
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On 1 November 2014 20:57, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > The dataset was generated by the generator in our internal benchmark project on Spark. Hope it will be open sourced later.
> > > >
> > > > 在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8下午1时39分05秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > > > On Wed, Oct 29, 2014 at 7:23 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > reduceByKey () currently supports setting of the number of partitions. I have changed the number of partitions when I was running the wordcount example.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > comparison with pySpark: on the same dataset, it takes pySpark ~35 seconds to complete. 2x slower than the native scala version. not so bad:)
> > > > > >
> > > > > Is this dataset available somewhere or is there a particular process to generate it ? It would be interesting to profile how much time is spent in different parts of SparkR to figure out where we can make improvements.
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks
> > > > > Shivaram
> > > > > > 在 2014年10月30日星期四UTC+8上午1时52分30秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > > > > > Thanks for benchmarking -- I think there are a couple of things here that affect performance, and can be improved.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > - Number of reducers: The default value gives bad performance and we should set the default number based on number of partitions in the previous RDD. Hao Lin actually did this for `distinct`, but we need to do it for reduceByKey as well.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > - Benchmark programs: One of the big bottlenecks in the word count example is that the performance of computing hashCode on strings is very slow. It would be great to also run Logistic Regression to get another data point which doesn't use string-keys for shuffle. (FYI The hashCode performance improvement is being tracked in https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-87)
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > - Comparison with Spark: While its useful to compare against Scala version of Spark, I think we should also compare with PySpark which has a similar architecture. That would help us figure out where our overheads are in SparkR code vs. the architecture decisions
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > Shivaram
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Tue, Oct 28, 2014 at 6:58 PM, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > It makes no sense to spark.driver.memory here. Use SPARK_MEM. In sparkR.R, you can see code:
> > > > > > > >   sparkMem <- Sys.getenv("SPARK_MEM", "512m")
> > > > > > > >   .sparkREnv$libname <- libname
> > > > > > > >   .sparkREnv$assemblyJarPath <- assemblyJarPath
> > > > > > > >   .jinit(classpath=assemblyJarPath, parameters=paste("-Xmx", sparkMem, sep=""))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > which picks SPARK_MEM to initialize the JVM max heap size when .jinit is called to launch a JVM.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 在 2014年10月29日星期三UTC+8上午7时14分14秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > > > > > I changed reduceByKey to take 10L and it now reduce time to half. Thank you very much for your help.
> > > > > > > > > I also tried to set driver memory using SPARK_MEM from command line but it not picking up that memory :
> > > > > > > > > SPARK_HOME=/usr/lib/spark SPARK_MEM=5g /home/user/SparkR-pkg-master/sparkR /home/userSparkR-pkg-master/examples/wordcount.R then I made changes in inti()
> > > > > > > > > inside code : sc <- sparkR.init(master="spark://master:7077", "SparkRWordCount100000kb", ,sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g")) this able to pick driver memory as spark env variables on each executor.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > also added cache(lines) to load data in memory
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > On 28 October 2014 14:24, <hipho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > Hi, Nahak,
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > currently SparkR is really slow. I ran the wordcount example with 3.2G data on a 3-slave spark cluster (16 logical CPUs and 48G memory per node) and it took 3.8 hours to complete. After I enabled map-side reduction, the time was shortened to 1.6 hours. While a scala version of wordcount only takes 17 seconds on the same dataset. You can try the following steps to see if the performance can be improved:
> > > > > > > > > > 1. Pull the latest code in which map-side reduction in reduceByKey() has been enabled;
> > > > > > > > > > 2. set driver memory using SPARK_MEM variable;
> > > > > > > > > > 3. Modify the wordcount source code:
> > > > > > > > > >   sc <- sparkR.init(args[[1]], "RwordCount", , sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory="3g"))
> > > > > > > > > > 4. Modify the wordcount source code to increase the reducer number for reduceByKey():
> > > > > > > > > >   counts <- reduceByKey(wordCount, "+", 10L)
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > 在 2014年10月28日星期二UTC+8上午8时44分36秒，Harihar Nahak写道：
> > > > > > > > > > > I was running a 100 MB file for wordcount given in sparkR examples and it took 1 hr 40 mins to complete. In same cluster when we compute MLllib SVD computation on 20 GB it completes on an hour. i.e.. spark clusters works as expected but same not with SparkR . Here is my cluster and app details , this might be a case :
> > > > > > > > > > >   >  1 master node of 16 GB memory with 4 cores {excluded from workers list}
> > > > > > > > > > >   >  3 workers,  Worker 1 has 4 cores/16g memory and Worker 2&3 have 2 cores/8g memory.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Environment settings: spark.executor.memory="3g", spark.driver.memory="5g" and reading input file from hdfs with 128 MB block size.
> > > > > > > > > > > screenshot of Worker 1 when application is running :
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > ​
> > > > > > > > > > > Any clue, is this the cluster issue or need to do something from R side?
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On 25 October 2014 01:52, hao lin <hlin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > I guess we could batch the R list partitions into smaller blocks, if necessary.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, October 23, 2014 10:44:20 PM UTC-4, hipho...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > It's OK to add persist(storageLevel) API to the RDD class. What I am concerned is that for large data sets, R worker may be a bottleneck because it loads the partition data entirely into memory as a list for processing. So if the partition data can't fit in memory in R worker, I am not sure about the behavior of R.
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > 在 2014年10月23日星期四UTC+8下午10时48分09秒，Shivaram Venkataraman写道：
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Right - using other storage levels isn't supported yet in SparkR. Could you file a JIRA issue to track this ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Shivaram
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Wed, Oct 22, 2014 at 9:49 PM, <hna...@wynyardgroup.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Just figure out , using cache() we can do this, but by default its store in MEMORY, how we can make it to MEMORY_AND_DISK? because I've more than 10 GB of file for processing.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, 23 October 2014 16:20:16 UTC+13, hna...@wynyardgroup.com wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I'm running SparkR on Apche Spark 1.1.0. while running workcount.R for 1 Gb input file, what I observed is it never store RDD in memory or disk. I checked in Executor tab which shows memory and disk used in each Executor, it always shows 0.0 B used.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In scala I can used rows.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)   , can we do the same thing in R as well ?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > --Harihar

messages.body_plain:
I'm just getting started with SparkR and having a few problems I'm hoping someone can help with. I'm running SparkR on an EC2 virtual cluster with 12 slave nodes, each with 2 VCPUs and about 8 Gb RAM. The EC2 cluster is started using the spark-ec2 script.

So far I can get a SparkR version of the pi calculation example working when I port code over from PySpark.

I can also load data in from HDFS and count the number of observations. E.g., here's what I am doing where I have about 12 Gb of data in 22 bzipped2 CSV files in /data/airline on HDFS. This works fine:
master <- system("cat /root/ephemeral-hdfs/conf/masters", intern = TRUE)
lines <- textFile(sc, paste0("hdfs://", master, ":9000/data/airline"))
count(lines)

##############################################
Problem #1

However, if I try to do:
take(lines, 1)

I get errors like this:
#14/11/13 02:32:01 WARN TaskSetManager: Lost task 0.2 in stage 5.0 (TID 52, ip-10-225-185-25.us-west-2.compute.internal): java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
# ....
#14/11/13 02:32:02 ERROR TaskSchedulerImpl: Lost executor 7 on ip-10-225-185-25.us-west-2.compute.internal: remote Akka client disassociated
...

##############################################
Problem #2

Also, if I try to do a map of the "lines" RDD, as follows,
createKeyValue <- function(line) {
  vals <- strsplit(line, ",")
  return(vals[1], line)
}
linesWithKey <- map(lines, createKeyValue)
count(linesWithKey)

I get errors like this:
14/11/13 03:25:16 WARN TaskSetManager: Lost task 0.0 in stage 2.0 (TID 33, ip-10-249-57-210.us-west-2.compute.internal): java.lang.NullPointerException:
        edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.RRDD.compute(RRDD.scala:128)
        org.apache.spark.rdd.RDD.computeOrReadCheckpoint(RDD.scala:262)
        org.apache.spark.rdd.RDD.iterator(RDD.scala:229)
        org.apache.spark.scheduler.ResultTask.runTask(ResultTask.scala:62)
        org.apache.spark.scheduler.Task.run(Task.scala:54)
        org.apache.spark.executor.Executor$TaskRunner.run(Executor.scala:177)
        java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1145)
        java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:615)
        java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:745)

#############################################
Problem #3

Finally, I noticed that SparkR seems to use /tmp on the slave nodes, putting large files there. On my EC2 cluster, / only has 7 Gb, while /mnt has 400 Gb. In one case /tmp was running out of disk space. I made a workaround of symlinking /tmp to /mnt/tmp, but I suspect there is a more elegant solution to this. Is there a standard way to deal with this in SparkR?

-Chris Paciorek

Statistical Computing Consultant
Statistical Computing Facility, Econometrics Lab, Berkeley Research Computing
UC Berkeley

Hi Chris,

Thanks for your reports!

- Problem 1: could you attach the stack trace under the line "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space"?

- Problem 2: I believe the problem is caused by the return() call in your closure. Changing it to list() (or c()) works for me:

    createKeyValue <- function(line) {
      vals <- strsplit(line, ",")

      list(vals[[1]], line)
    }

Currently if key-value RDDs are to be used, it should be a list or vector. I also changed [1] to [[1]], but this may depend on your application's semantics.

- Problem 3: could you post the file names of those temp files? If they are indeed SparkR's tmp files then we'd need to look into it. Otherwise if they are Spark's temp files, then setting `spark.local.dir` [1] to a desired location might help (you can pass in this configuration option in sparkR.init()).

[1] http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html#application-properties

Zongheng

messages.body_plain:
Couple of additional points to what Zongheng said

1. For the Java heap space issue, are you passing the amount of executor memory to use ? The default Spark uses is pretty low (I think 512MB) and you can increase it by passing 'spark.executor.memory' in the spark context constructor. An example is shown in https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/blob/master/README.md

3. You are right that SparkR uses tmp files during its processing. Where the tmp files are stored can be configured. You can set 'spark.local.dir' to '/mnt' in the Spark Context constructor (the same one we used above) and that should do the trick

Even better would be to use a memory mounted filesystem like tmpfs. [1] has some instructions on how to mount tmpfs at /tmp

Thanks
Shivaram

[1] http://www.jamescoyle.net/how-to/943-create-a-ram-disk-in-linux

messages.body_plain:
Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> created an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-136> SPARKR-136 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-136>
SparkR should use SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-136>
Issue Type:    Bug
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   Internals
Created:   13/Nov/14 11:55 AM
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram>

Right now SparkR only looks at the variable spark.local.dirs and java.io.tmpdir. We should also use the environment variable SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS as it is used in Spark.

Relevant code snippet from Utils.scala in Spark below
      Option(conf.getenv("SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS")).getOrElse(
        conf.get("spark.local.dir", System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir")))

messages.body_plain:
It is called SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS in Spark (as documented in [1]) and you can also set this in spark-env.sh. However there is a limitation in SparkR where we don't read this environment variable right now. I've created a bug to fix this at https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-136

Right now I can think of two solutions for you:

1.  I think the easiest thing would be for you to create the SparkContext manually in your file instead of using the script SparkR. All you need to do for that is to add these two lines at the top of your file
    library(SparkR) // Pass in lib.loc if SparkR is installed somewhere not in libPaths
    sc <- sparkR.init(master=Sys.getenv("MASTER") ... )

2. You can modify the script `sparkR` to read the environment variable SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS and pass it on as spark.local.dirs.

I can send you a patch for the second one if that will be useful.

Thanks
Shivaram

messages.body_plain:
Sure, the patch might be helpful. I'm thinking about what is easiest
to do in terms of giving instructions to who might use it...

One thing to consider here is that with PySpark I haven't had to worry
either about changing the memory or about space on /tmp. If there's a
way to have SparkR handle things as PySpark does, that might be good.
Is PySpark somehow not making as heavy use of /tmp, since I haven't
run into the disk space issue with PySpark?

On Thu, Nov 13, 2014 at 11:58 AM, Shivaram Venkataraman
<shivaram.v...@gmail.com> wrote:
> It is called SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS in Spark (as documented in [1]) and you can
> also set this in spark-env.sh. However there is a limitation in SparkR where
> we don't read this environment variable right now. I've created a bug to fix
> this at https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-136
>
> Right now I can think of two solutions for you:
>
> 1.  I think the easiest thing would be for you to create the SparkContext
> manually in your file instead of using the script SparkR. All you need to do
> for that is to add these two lines at the top of your file
>     library(SparkR) // Pass in lib.loc if SparkR is installed somewhere not
> in libPaths
>     sc <- sparkR.init(master=Sys.getenv("MASTER") ... )
>
> 2. You can modify the script `sparkR` to read the environment variable
> SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS and pass it on as spark.local.dirs.
>
> I can send you a patch for the second one if that will be useful.
>
> Thanks
> Shivaram
> On Thu Nov 13 2014 at 11:43:54 AM <paci...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
>>
>> Shivaram, thanks, this looks very helpful.
>>
>> However, one question - I'm starting SparkR via the SparkR script, so I'm
>> not actually calling sparkR.init(). I can start sparkR with SPARK_MEM
>> variable set, but is there a SPARK_LOCAL_DIR environment variable as well?
>> I assume so, but if you could let me know the exact name, that would be
>> helpful.
>>
>>

>>> constructor. An example is shown in
>>> https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/blob/master/README.md

>>> the tmp files are stored can be configured. You can set 'spark.local.dir' to
>>> '/mnt' in the Spark Context constructor (the same one we used above) and

>>> has some instructions on how to mount tmpfs at /tmp

>>>> location might help (you can pass in this configuration option in

messages.body_plain:
PySpark uses sockets instead of temporary files, so it doesn't directly run into this problem.

Regarding the latest error, I think this is because the driver memory isn't enough to collect the output from take. Could you set the env variable SPARK_MEM in addition to passing spark.executor.memory ? SPARK_MEM ensures that the driver JVM also gets enough memory

Shivaram

So once it's merged, can I start SparkR using the SparkR script and skipping sparkR.init and skip setting spark.executor.memory, so long as I set SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS and SPARK_MEM when I call the SparkR script? Or should I be setting SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS and SPARK_MEM when I start R and setting spark.executor.memry when I call sparkR.init?

>
> Thanks

messages.subject_clean: having problems with basic dataset manipulation
messages.body_plain:
Once its merged you can directly use the sparkR script with SPARK_MEM set in the environment. Note that SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS needs to be present in the environment in the workers, which is why it needs to be in spark-env.sh (it should be there by default).

Also in your case of providing instructions to use SparkR, I think its always nice to tell people both ways of doing things. sparkR script is easier to use, but its meant as an example (similar to spark-shell in Scala). In general I think it better for users to just create the SparkContext in their R program and call Rscript <program.R>

Thanks
Shivaram

Hi Zongheng,

I've tested my code again and things seem to be good now with the new patch. I'm setting SPARK_MEM before calling SparkR. SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS is indeed in spark-env.sh on the slaves.

A few comments/suggestions about the EC2 SparkR instructions.

1) I needed to tell R about the Java configuration using R CMD javareconf. So this is what I ran on the master node to get SparkR set up. You might add the "R CMD javareconf" to the SparkR wiki instructions on EC2. Also as a minor note, why do you untar the rJava tarball before installing on the master. You can just pass the tarball to "R CMD INSTALL" unless I'm missing something here.

cd /root
wget http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/src/contrib/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
R CMD javareconf
tar xvzf rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz; R CMD INSTALL rJava
/root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD javareconf; R CMD INSTALL ~/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz

cd /root
git clone https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg.git
cd SparkR-pkg
./install-dev.sh
/root/spark-ec2/copy-dir /root/SparkR-pkg

2) Is there a way for SparkR to intelligently query the memory on the workers instead of having the low default memory? If not, I'd suggest adding to the SparkR wiki on EC2 that one should do:

MASTER=`cat /root/spark-ec2/cluster-url` SPARK_MEM=XXXg ./sparkR

where XXX will depend on the instance types.

3) This didn't seem to matter to SparkR, but I noticed that if I load rJava in an R session on a slave node, I get this error in finding libjvm.so. For some reason R has no problem finding libjvm.so on the master.

> library(rJava)
Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rJava', details:
  call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
  error: unable to load shared object '/usr/lib64/R/library/rJava/libs/rJava.so':
  libjvm.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘rJava’

-chris

Chris,

Thanks a lot for your feedback. Some replies inline

On Tue, Nov 18, 2014 at 7:54 PM, <paci...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi Zongheng,
>
> I've tested my code again and things seem to be good now with the new patch. I'm setting SPARK_MEM before calling SparkR. SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS is indeed in spark-env.sh on the slaves.
>
> A few comments/suggestions about the EC2 SparkR instructions.
>
> 1) I needed to tell R about the Java configuration using R CMD javareconf. So this is what I ran on the master node to get SparkR set up. You might add the "R CMD javareconf" to the SparkR wiki instructions on EC2. Also as a minor note, why do you untar the rJava tarball before installing on the master. You can just pass the tarball to "R CMD INSTALL" unless I'm missing something here.
>
> cd /root
> wget http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/src/contrib/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
> /root/spark-ec2/copy-dir rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
> R CMD javareconf
> tar xvzf rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz; R CMD INSTALL rJava
> /root/spark/sbin/slaves.sh R CMD javareconf; R CMD INSTALL ~/rJava_0.9-6.tar.gz
>
> cd /root
> git clone https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg.git
> cd SparkR-pkg
> ./install-dev.sh
> /root/spark-ec2/copy-dir /root/SparkR-pkg
>

Good point about the R CMD javareconf -- We will add that to the wiki. And you are right, we dont need to un-tar the rJava package which should reduce one step.

> 2) Is there a way for SparkR to intelligently query the memory on the workers instead of having the low default memory? If not, I'd suggest adding to the SparkR wiki on EC2 that one should do:
>
> MASTER=`cat /root/spark-ec2/cluster-url` SPARK_MEM=XXXg ./sparkR
>
> where XXX will depend on the instance types.
>

There is a bug here that SparkR doesn't read the spark-defaults.conf file during startup. I've filed a JIRA to track this at https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141 -- In the meantime we can just change our example specify SPARK_MEM.

> 3) This didn't seem to matter to SparkR, but I noticed that if I load rJava in an R session on a slave node, I get this error in finding libjvm.so. For some reason R has no problem finding libjvm.so on the master.
>
> > library(rJava)
> Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rJava', details:
>   call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
>   error: unable to load shared object '/usr/lib64/R/library/rJava/libs/rJava.so':
>   libjvm.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
> Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘rJava’
>
>
> -chris
>
>
> On Friday, November 14, 2014 8:03:52 PM UTC-8, Zongheng Yang wrote:
> > Oops, I meant to directly link to the Github PR: https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/108

> > > I just created a related patch that might solve the take() OOM issue for you: <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-139>. Could you give this a try and see if things improve? With this fix I think the driver memory needs not be increased.
> > >
> > > Thanks,
> > > Zongheng
> > >
> > > On Thu Nov 13 2014 at 3:48:25 PM Shivaram Venkataraman <shivaram.v...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Once its merged you can directly use the sparkR script with SPARK_MEM set in the environment. Note that SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS needs to be present in the environment in the workers, which is why it needs to be in spark-env.sh (it should be there by default).
> > > >
> > > > Also in your case of providing instructions to use SparkR, I think its always nice to tell people both ways of doing things. sparkR script is easier to use, but its meant as an example (similar to spark-shell in Scala). In general I think it better for users to just create the SparkContext in their R program and call Rscript <program.R>

Kien Dang <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=kien_dang> commented on  SPARKR-131 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-131>

Re: Have the ability to create and return a LabeledPoint RDD to be used with MLlib <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-131>

I manage to use MLlib in SparkR by getting the underlying JavaRDD of a R RDD of type labeledpoint(numeric, numeric vector) (using SparkR:::getJRDD) then converting it to a Scala RDD of type LabeledPoint and passing it to the MLlib function using rJava:

SparkR's Naive Bayes example https://gist.github.com/kiendang/4d73612ce35cbf943b0f
Scala code to convert types https://gist.github.com/kiendang/4aef5fb0c249613dec65

But in order to do so, I have to use Rserve to use the R unserialize function in the step where I convert a Scala RDD of serialized R objects to a Scala RDD of Scala LabeledPoint. I understand that I may call the R interpreter instead of Rserve but I'm not sure how.

Currently my company is working on integration of SparkR and Spark's MLlib. I'm thinking of adding a new discussion to move this forward and would love to hear your opinions.

Kien Dang <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=kien_dang> I will take a look at your code, it looks really nice. Perhaps Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui> had a good point in the earlier comment regarding py4j, which I think the R equivalent is Rengine. In my opinion there are two paradigms, either R is called from within the Java code, in which case the unserialization takes place there or, something like the python Pickler class and unserialization takes place before the conversion to labeledPoint. Maybe my earlier thinking of trying to avoid calling R within Java was wrong. Then again SparkR makes use of Rscript, so I wonder is there a difference between using Rscript and Rengine? Considering that instead of Java calling R explicitly with Rengine, SparkR is calling R implicitly with Rscript.

My idea was lapply would be called first to put the data into a label/vector format then the output could be converted to a labeledPoint format before being passed to the MLlib function.

hao <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=hlin> updated an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-142> SPARKR-142 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-142>
Function dependencies are captured too late, so that the value of free variables have already changed <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-142>

Change By:   hao <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=hlin>
The function dependencies is computed when JRDD is constructed. However, this should be done when PipelinedRDD is created. Otherwise, there is possibility that the values of free variables have already changed.

E.g.
rdd <- parallelize(...)
free.var <- 1
rdd1 <- lapply(rdd, function(x) { x + free.var } )
free.var <- 2
rdd2 <- lapply(rdd, function(x) { x + free.var} )
collect(rdd1)
collect(rdd2)

The result is wrong since both rdd1 and rdd2 will have free.var == 2, since free.var is updated before rdd1 is evaluated.

Suggested Solution: Maybe we can add a "depsBin" in the PipelinedRDD object, and compute the dependencies once the PipelinedRDD is created.

hao <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=hlin> This is a good point and this behavior could be unintuitive to users. I think your proposal of having a depsBin per RDD is along the right lines – However I think this change is a bit tricky as in worker.R we'll need to load the right env for each RDD we evaluate (we only load one depsBin globally at the beginning right now).

FWIW I think the behavior is broken in Scala too (I just checked a similar code path to what you posted) and there have been efforts to fix this in https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-729 but they haven't been merged.
